title: Competition and Consumer Amendment (Safeguarding the Reputation of Australian Beef) Bill 2017
short_title: Competition and Consumer Amendment (Safeguarding the Reputation of Australian Beef) Bill 2017

speeches.speaker: Rebekha Sharkie
speeches.brief: The speaker moved the second reading of the Competition and Consumer Amendment (Safeguarding the Reputation of Australian Beef) Bill, which would make it illegal to market beef as "Australian" unless it was processed under Australian standards and within Australia. The bill proposes maximum fines of $1.1 million for companies and $220,000 for individuals to protect the reputation of the Australian beef industry, which was worth $22.9 billion in the last year and supports 35,000 direct and 100,000 indirect jobs.
